lane_fabric_b_round_1.verdict_verbatim:
VERDICT: APPROVE
REVIEWER: independent executor-lane reviewer (non-author)
REVIEWED_DIFF: git diff HEAD @ ab98c9df5 restricted to tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app/src/lib.rs, tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app/tests/contract.rs
RATIONALE: The canonical-name guard in FsFlowMetricsStore::pass_seqs is genuinely fail-closed: every id reaching the check parses to a u64, and acceptance requires exact string equality with format!("pass-{seq:020}"), so the accepted set is precisely the canonical rendering — no numeric alias (pass-7, pass-007, 21-digit padding, "+"-prefixed parse quirk) can bump the monotonic head while staying invisible to pass()/passes(). Overflow digits (e.g. 20 nines > u64::MAX) and uppercase PASS- fail u64 parse / prefix strip and hit the intact pre-existing foreign-file rejection. The regression test provably fails against the old behavior: old pass_seqs would admit seq 7, making passes() return Ok (not Corrupt) and record_pass(seq 2) return NonMonotonicPass (not Corrupt) — both matches! assertions would trip. Diff within the declared surface is confined to pass_seqs plus the one new test; cargo test -p oya-fabric-loop-state-app (27 passed, incl. non_canonical_pass_filenames_are_refused_fail_closed) and cargo clippy --all-targets are green.
FINDINGS:
- [minor] tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app/src/lib.rs:1507-1512 - Pre-existing (out of this diff): list_json_ids silently skips filenames that fail validate_id (unicode digits, spaces, '+', non-UTF-8 names) instead of erroring. These are symmetrically invisible (they influence neither the head nor reads), so no head/content divergence is possible, but a strict fail-closed ledger would surface them as Corrupt too. Worth a follow-up card, not blocking this change.
- [nit] tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app/src/lib.rs:1749 - format!("pass-{seq:020}") allocates per entry; a width/leading-zero string comparison (id.len()==25-prefix check) could avoid it, but ledger dirs are small and clarity wins. No action needed.

lane_fabric_c_round_1.verdict_verbatim:
VERDICT: APPROVE
REVIEWER: independent executor-lane reviewer (non-author)
REVIEWED_DIFF: git diff HEAD @ ab98c9df5 restricted to tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app/src/main.rs
RATIONALE: The CliError::Usage/Plane split reroutes exactly the four declared operator-usage paths (verify-done arity, define-card required flags, malformed --timeline, malformed --surface) and nothing store-related: every facade call (claim/start/heartbeat/block/complete/verify_done/record_next_pass/check_lane_disjointness) maps to CliError::Plane, whose Display forwards PlaneError text verbatim (pinned by test). Exit-code behavior is unchanged (all errors funnel through fail() -> FAILURE; success paths -> SUCCESS), the check-disjoint JSON report print and overlap-fails gate are byte-for-byte untouched, success-path stdout strings are unchanged, and the fail-closed now_epoch_s clock refusal is intact and still prints raw PlaneError text. Verified independently: 6 new bin unit tests pass (27 total across 3 suites), scoped clippy clean, and the main.rs change has no dependency on the sibling lanes' uncommitted lib.rs/contract.rs edits (PlaneError already derives Clone/PartialEq/Eq at HEAD ab98c9df5).
FINDINGS:
- [minor] tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app/src/main.rs:259 - Malformed --kind (BlockKind::parse), --phase (DisjointnessPhase::parse at :425), and non-numeric --reviewer-capacity (:426) are also operator-usage class but still surface as PlaneError text without the usage prefix. Outside the declared intent scope, so non-blocking; worth a follow-up card for consistency.
- [nit] tools/oya-fabric-loop-state-app/src/main.rs:539 - Tests pin the CliError type per path but do not exercise the full main() dispatch (e.g. that block/complete errors carry no usage prefix end-to-end); acceptable given the bin-local helpers cover the rerouted logic.
